pages.text: Shannon's source coding theorem: a source of entropy H bits per symbol can be compressed to any rate R above H - and to none below. At finite block length n, the error falls as exp(−n(R−H)²/2V). Every concept has its own entropy.
$(thing)Set$(): Code rate R, Block length n, Store field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Source drift: the concept's entropy fluctuates by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Rate below the entropy: information is destroyed; Store field too weak for that rate; Interlock: holographic-store coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the holographic-store coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter blocks compress faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Entropy H: H = −q log q − (1−q) log(1−q)$(br)Dispersion V: V = q(1−q)·log²((1−q)/q)$(br)Rate margin R − H: R − H$(br)Error probability: P_e ≈ exp(−n(R−H)²/2V)$(br)Compression ratio: 1/R$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)
